::: {.callout-note}
**This document is for the facilitator's eyes only.** It is rendered with the site but left out of the navbar, so nothing on the site links to it. It holds the run sheets, the answer keys, the crib facts and the contingency ladders of the one-day workshop of the EU-frames case (`slides/eu-frames-one-day.qmd`), which works on aggregate data only and is taught mainly in the browser lab, and the sessions of the Extended course, whose second day is the workshop. The pages of a format give the participants no times, and every time is here. The decks, the browser lab, the class chart and the other notes on the formats are in the section on [the decks and the pipeline](#decks-and-pipeline).
:::

## The formats {#the-three-formats}

The facilitator chooses the format; participants do not choose, and the home page describes the formats without offering a choice. Each track is an ordered route through pages that already exist on the site, with a docked sidebar of its own (`_sidebar.yml`) and a slides page embedding the deck it runs on. Name the track of a delivery in `delivery.track` of `_variables.yml`, and the callout of the home page links it. The decisions behind the formats, and the order in which their material was built, are in `_planning/formats-2026-10-27.md` of the course repository, and the old addresses of the three one-day focuses of October 2026 and of the three-day course forward to the pages of the formats through `aliases:`.

| Format | Track | What it holds | Deck |
|---|---|---|---|
| Short session | `tracks/eu-frames-short/` | Two halves of eighty and ninety minutes in the browser lab: the three Rs and Multi100, the paper and its record, the estimand statement, the reproduction of C6HJR or KQXUE, the three models and few clusters; then the menu with its survey decisions first, the code behind the menu, Task 4 and the class chart, the multiverse and the curve of 864, reading a curve, the critics and preregistration, and the replication by its verdict | `slides/eu-frames-short.qmd`, a deck written for the session |
| One-day workshop | `tracks/eu-frames-one-day/` | Four parts: the claim and credibility, the estimand and the causal graph, the reproduction, and robustness with Tasks 4 and 5 | `slides/eu-frames-one-day.qmd` |
| Extended course | `tracks/eu-frames-extended/` | Day 1 open research and the tools, the same for every case; day 2 the workshop; day 3 the methods of the case and the report of each participant | the decks of day 1 on the AR4DS site, `slides/eu-frames-one-day.qmd` on day 2, and the decks of day 3 |
| Self-study | `tracks/self-study/` | Five stages, from credibility and the three Rs to a project of your own | the full deck, `slides/eu-frames-full.qmd` |

The workshop works on aggregate data only and is taught mainly in the browser lab. Its parts are of unequal length: the reproduction is the shortest, and robustness the longest, because it holds the two tasks with submissions. The clock times below are drafts; set them for the delivery and paste them into the day plan and the joining instructions, because the pages of the participants give no times.

| Segment | Clock (GMT, draft) |
|---|---|
| Part 1 | 10:00–11:30 |
| Break | 11:30–12:00 |
| Part 2 | 12:00–13:15 |
| Lunch | 13:15–14:15 |
| Part 3 | 14:15–15:25 |
| Break | 15:25–15:55 |
| Part 4 | 15:55–17:45 |

## The delivery lifecycle {#delivery-lifecycle}

Between deliveries the landing page advertises no upcoming delivery. Scheduling a delivery takes the steps below, and resetting after one takes two.

**Scheduling.**

- [ ] Fill the `delivery:` block in `_variables.yml` (date, venue or platform, event, mode, registration URL), set `track` to `eu-frames-one-day` or `eu-frames-extended`, and set `active: 'true'`. Re-render and push, and the landing page shows a "Next delivery" callout. Set `active: 'false'` again afterwards.
- [ ] Decide recording. If recording: talk segments only, announced at the start of each recorded stretch, paused for hands-on and chat-heavy segments. Nothing in the day depends on the recording either way.
- [ ] Optionally create the preregistration mirror form from `_planning/prereg-form-spec.md` and paste its URL into `_variables.yml`. The preregistration block is the primary record and the form only a backup, so skipping the form loses nothing.

**Resetting, after a workshop.**

- [ ] Export the responses Sheet (File → Download → CSV) and commit it as a date-stamped snapshot (for example `cases/eu-frames/data/class_results_2026-11-06.csv`); refresh `cases/eu-frames/data/class_results.csv` as `facilitator/live-results-setup.md` describes if you want the archived class visible on the site.
- [ ] Clear (or archive to a second tab) the old rows in the live Sheet so that the chart opens almost empty for the next class. **Do not touch the Form, the Worker, or the field schema.** The pipeline works, and only the rows change from one class to the next.

## The preparation of participants {#preparation}

The page "Before the day" or "Before the course" of each format lists these steps. The pages give no times, so if the joining instructions need them, put them there.

| Step | One-day workshop | Extended course |
|---|---|---|
| The case study | required | required |
| The browser lab, opened once, with the cells of Task 1 run (the R engine takes 10 to 30 seconds to load on a slow connection) | required | – |
| R, an IDE and the workspace, until `R/check_setup.R` reports no failure | required | required |
| Getting started with R (`tools/r.qmd` on the AR4DS site) | required | required |
| The Eurobarometer files, downloaded under a GESIS account of the participant | – | required |
| The exercise overview, sections 1 to 3 of the module on panel data, and Reading a specification curve (`cases/eu-frames/reading-inference.qmd`) | recommended | – |
| The modules on the IDE, on Quarto and on Git and GitHub (AR4DS site) | recommended | the reading of days 1 and 3 |

## The week before

- [ ] Send joining instructions: the before-the-day page of the track, the browser-lab link with the instruction to open it once, the two-window or two-device tip, and the [case study](../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd) as the pre-reading. For the workshop and the Extended course add the setup page, with the request to run `R/check_setup.R` until it reports no failure, and the module Getting started with R; for the Extended course add the download of the Eurobarometer files.
- [ ] Confirm that the four Task 2 instructions on the Part 3 slide "Task 2 of Multi100" match your own Task 2 report (copy in `_planning/osf_source/moreh_rep_vAPR2025/`), which is the source that the slide quotes.
- [ ] Check that the three OSF deposits of Hands-on 3b load logged out (osf.io/vycgd, osf.io/nz7ka, osf.io/6zqct), and that osf.io/h7432 shows the five Multi100 components.
- [ ] Click once through the tab switching of Part 4 (deck, the specification menu, the decision map, the Multiverse page and back), so that the order is familiar on the day.

## The night before

- [ ] Render the site and push; if the site is published, confirm that the Pages build completes on GitHub Actions.
- [ ] **Browser lab cold load**: open the live page of `cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd` in a private window on the connection typical of the venue; time the load of the webR engine; run the cells of Task 1 and the cells of all three analysts in Task 3. The cell of 018OL that installs lme4 and lmerTest downloads about 32 MB, so time that too.
- [ ] **The live results loop** (full setup and checks in `facilitator/live-results-setup.md`): submit one anonymous test row through the Form in a private window, confirm that it reaches the Sheet and that the Worker returns the sheet as CSV, press *Run Code* on the live [Multiverse]({{< var live-results-url >}}) page and find the test mark. Then delete the test row.
- [ ] **The preregistration loop**: complete the preregistration cell of the browser lab with a dummy specification, run `prereg()`, `build_model()` and `run_spec()`, and check the output. If the mirror form exists, submit one dummy row and delete it.
- [ ] Prepare the catch-up card, the help document and the day plan (texts below) as snippets ready to paste.
- [ ] Charge everything; sign a second device in to the meeting as a participant, to check what the class sees.

## Opening the room {#opening-the-virtual-room--30-minutes-before}

- [ ] Open the meeting early; enable chat for everyone; check that breakout rooms are available (they are optional – nothing depends on them).
- [ ] Seed the chat with the site URL, the browser-lab URL, the cheatsheet URL and the day plan with its times (the standing order if the host drops: "follow the day plan; finish the current task or take the break early; I will rejoin").
- [ ] Post the interaction key: "green circle = working; STUCK = I need help; answers to quizzes: type but hold until I say go".
- [ ] Share the deck; keep the browser lab ready in a second tab (also the specification menu, the decision map and the Multiverse page).
- [ ] If recording: announce it now and state what is and is not recorded.

## Driving the decks {#deck-navigation}

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| space, right arrow, clicker | next slide. **Always exactly one slide** – the decks are set to linear mode so that no clicker press can skip a segment |
| **`d`** | switch between the **full** and the **lean** deck, live. In lean mode the optional slides are taken out of the deck: every key skips them and the count drops |
| **`]`** and **`[`** | jump to the **next or previous part** |
| **`g`** | **jump bar**: type a few letters of any slide title, press Enter |
| **`s`** | speaker view (notes, timer, next slide) |
| **`f`**, **`esc`** | fullscreen, slide overview |

**The readout, top right,** has two lines. The first names the part and gives the position in the part and in the deck (for example `PART 3`, `8/24`, `90/148`). The second is a badge that is always present and shows the state of the deck:

| Badge | Means |
|---|---|
| green **full** | the optional runs are switched on, and this slide is part of the main flow |
| burgundy **optional** | the optional runs are switched on, and this slide belongs to one of them. The figure beside it is your position inside that run – `3/12` |
| amber **lean** | the optional runs are switched off |
| a burgundy **dot** before the amber badge | lean mode, and an optional run has been lifted out right here – either the slide you are on is the last before it, or the first after it. Press `d` if the class wants it |

The one-day deck lifts no optional run into its main flow (`core-runs: []`), and the full deck lifts both runs, the methodological tutorial and the multiverse tutorial; add `?depth=0` to the address to open a deck in lean mode. The first slide of each optional run has a small grey link at the top right, which says how many slides the run contains and where the main flow resumes.

## The decks and the pipeline {#decks-and-pipeline}

**The browser lab.** The browser lab is a page that runs R in the tab of the browser and holds the five tasks of the exercise beside the workspace. It is live: it loads the data of the case, which are small (a panel of 43 KB), and runs the code of the tasks on them, each fit in a fraction of a second, so the workshop is taught in it. The causal-graph task prints the answers that the pipeline computed with dagitty for the graphs that the cell offers, because dagitty cannot run in the tab; any other graph goes to the workspace.

**The decks.** The decks are assembled from the segments in `slides/_segments/eu-frames/`. A deck is a list of `{{< include >}}` lines with its own agenda, aims and part dividers. In the segment files, every slide of an optional run is marked with `.deepdive` and a `run` attribute (`methods` or `multiverse`). A deck lists the runs that belong to its main flow under `core-runs:` in its YAML, and `slides/core-runs.lua` strips the `.deepdive` mark from those headings, so `nav-tools.html` neither hides them on the `d` key nor badges them as optional. A run that is not listed stays optional: it is hidden in lean mode and has the escape-hatch link on its first slide. The segment files contain R chunks with labels, and knitr refuses a duplicate label, so each deck includes each segment at most once. Edit the segment files for content, or the deck file for order and framing, and render the deck on its own (`quarto render slides/eu-frames-one-day.qmd`). A change to a segment needs every deck that includes it rendered again (`grep -l "eu-frames/_x.qmd" slides/*.qmd`). The project render fails at its final move step on this machine, so decks are rendered one at a time.

**The short session.** The short session is three hours in two halves, entirely in the browser lab, with no Task 2 at the keyboard (the estimand statement is a held answer), no Task 5, and one submission to the class chart, the explored analysis of Task 4. Its deck, `slides/eu-frames-short.qmd`, is not assembled from the segments of the one-day deck: it is a custom set of slides in `slides/_segments/eu-frames-short/`, one segment for each block of the run, with the clock of the block in a comment at the head of the segment, so that an event can edit the deck block by block and set its own title and subtitle in the YAML. The reproduction offers C6HJR and KQXUE, because the packages of 018OL download 32 MB in the lab. A live version of the deck, `live/eu-frames-short.qmd`, carries the cells of Tasks 1, 3 and 4 on its slides through the Quarto Live extension, so that a delivery can run inside one deck with the lab as the fallback; it lives in a folder of its own with `live/_metadata.yml` keyed `live-revealjs`, because the `format: revealjs` key of the metadata of `slides/` would render it twice (root notes, Gotchas), and both decks include the same segments except the hands-on ones. The helpers of the lab (`try_spec()` and the rest) are one file, `cases/eu-frames/_lab-helpers.qmd`, included by the lab and by the live deck. The first delivery proposed is the ESRA–WAPOR conference of July 2027 in Paris, for an audience of survey researchers, which is why the menu is taught with its survey decisions first and two slides show the easystats code behind the course. The [run sheet](#run-sheet-short) gives the clock.

**Pages that the formats share.** Every track starts from the [case study](../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd), which tells the original study, SCORE and Multi100, the five reanalysts with an assessment of their choices, and the conversion lesson on how Multi100 turned their statistics into one effect size. The specification menu is taught as the full set of fourteen decisions, on the [decision map](../cases/eu-frames/map.qmd) and the [specification menu](../cases/eu-frames/menu.qmd), with the curve of 864 specifications as the subset that an audit judged justifiable for this claim. The helpers of the browser lab and of the workspace refuse an option that is off the curve, with the one-sentence reason recorded in `data/menu_options.csv` and the page that teaches the option. Every result is classed by standard errors clustered by country with the CR2 correction and Satterthwaite degrees of freedom; the specification of C6HJR (t = −3.804, r = −0.242) has a CR2 p of 0.0504 on 9.8 degrees of freedom and is not significant under that rule, which is worth saying before anyone asks. The [run sheet of the one-day workshop](#run-sheet-one-day) has its timings.

**The class chart.** The chart on the Multiverse page reads the rows of the shared results Form whose labels have the frozen format of the case, `explore: [tag] <spec>` or `declared: [tag] <spec>`, with no case word after the tag. The labels of the other cases of AR4DS carry the case word, and the chart draws their rows as unclassed diamonds, so clear the Sheet between deliveries of different cases. Each workspace keeps its own tag in `.class-tag`, so ask a cohort to choose one nickname and to pass it as `nickname = "..."` throughout. A chart keeps the rows of earlier deliveries until the sheet is cleared.

## Run sheet – the short session {#run-sheet-short}

The short session runs on `slides/eu-frames-short.qmd`, a deck written for it, as two halves of eighty and ninety minutes with a break of ten, entirely in the browser lab. It has no Task 2 at the keyboard (the estimand statement is a held answer), no Task 5, and one submission to the class chart, the explored analysis of Task 4; the reproduction offers C6HJR and KQXUE. In a room the held answers go on cards or a shared pad named on the first slide, and the class chart stays on the projector from Task 4 to the close. Ask participants to open the lab the evening before on the machine they bring, so that the browser holds its files, and carry a phone hotspot. A delivery on the live deck (`live/eu-frames-short.qmd`) asks the same of the deck: participants open it the evening before, and during the session they run the cells on the hands-on slides while the facilitator drives the same deck on the projector; the rows of the run sheet are the same, with Hands-on 1 on two slides (one for each analyst) and Hands-on 2 on three (the reference call, two variations, the submission). Clear the results Sheet before the session.

### Cutting order and never cut {#cuts-short}

For a slot of two and a half hours, cut in this order: the slide on where the idea of the multiverse comes from; the critics to one slide; the three models to one; the record in SCORE at speed; the code behind the menu to one slide. **Never cut:** the five results, the held estimand statement, the reproduction and its held answer, Task 4 with the class chart, the bet before the decomposition, and robustness against replicability on this paper.

### Cutting order and never cut {#cuts-one-day}

- **Part 1** – trigger 0:24: the open-research practices table in one sentence per row.
- **Part 2** – trigger 0:18: the crash course drops the selection-and-feedback slide to a sentence. Trigger 1:08: Task 2 to demonstration only.
- **Part 3** – trigger 0:30: the three reproduced models in one slide. Trigger 0:52: Hands-on 3b on my screen.
- **Part 4** – trigger 0:10: the methodological tutorial stays off, or keeps its core slides (outcome, claim alignment, estimators, what fixed effects adjust for). Trigger 0:20: Task 4 shortens to two `try_spec()` calls and a submission – but everybody still submits. Trigger 0:38: skip the multiverse tutorial, keep "what the curve leaves out". Trigger 1:17: the replication and the critics in one slide each.

**Never cut:** the five-analyst reveal; the estimand waterfall; the half-built graph and its adjustment set; the reproduction waterfall; the table of CR2 tests; the Task 4 submission; the bet before the decomposition; the preregistration moment.

## The Extended course {#run-extended}

The Extended course is three days, with the one-day workshop as its second day (`tracks/eu-frames-extended/`). The first day is the same for every case of AR4DS and is given from decks of the AR4DS site; the third day teaches the methods of this case, from the panel to the respondents, and ends with the report of each participant. A two-day version drops the third day. Participants download the Eurobarometer files before the course, under their own GESIS accounts. At the end of the second day the participants start the build of the file of respondents in the workspace, with `prep/01_build_respondents.R`, and let it finish that evening, so that a check that fails comes to light while the facilitator can still help; the second session of the third day starts from the built file.

::: {.callout-note}
Each session of the first and the third days has a deck of its own, written on 6 November 2026 and not yet tried in class, and a module as its reading. The first day teaches R, the IDE and Quarto in the workspace of the housing-audit case, the running example of the modules, so the participants install it beside the workspace of this case. The durations are drafts for CM to adjust.
:::

**Day 1 – Open research and the tools.**

| Session | Deck, AR4DS site | Reading | Draft |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Credibility and the three Rs | `slides/credibility.qmd` | the glossary of `resources.qmd` | 75′ |
| 2. SCORE and Multi100 | `slides/score-multi100.qmd` | the pages on SCORE and Multi100 and on the Multi100 article, AR4DS site | 60′ |
| 3. Repositories and data sources | `slides/repositories.qmd` | `companion/data-sources.qmd`, `companion/repositories.qmd` | 60′ |
| 4. R | `slides/r.qmd` | `tools/r.qmd` on the AR4DS site, `companion/intro-r.qmd` | 75′ |
| 5. Positron | `slides/ide.qmd` | `tools/ide.qmd` on the AR4DS site, `companion/ide.qmd` | 45′ |
| 6. Quarto | `slides/quarto.qmd` | `tools/quarto.qmd` on the AR4DS site | 60′ |

**Day 2 – The workshop**, run as in its own run sheet above. After the first day, Part 1 can take credibility and Multi100 at speed and give the time to Task 1 and Task 2. The day ends with the start of the build, as the section "Before day 3" of the day page sets out: each participant puts the sixteen files in one folder beside the workspace, sources `prep/01_build_respondents.R` before leaving and reports any check that fails, with `data_private/build_report.csv`.

**Day 3 – The methods and your report.**

| Session | Deck | Reading | Draft |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Panel data | `slides/eu-frames-panel-data.qmd` | `companion/panel-data.qmd` | 75′ |
| 2. Multilevel models and the respondents, on the file built after day 2 | `slides/eu-frames-multilevel.qmd` | `companion/multilevel.qmd` | 75′ |
| 3. Bayesian estimation | `slides/eu-frames-bayesian.qmd` | `companion/bayesian.qmd` | 60′ |
| 4. Your report | `slides/eu-frames-report.qmd` | `git-github.qmd` and `tools/quarto.qmd`, AR4DS site | 120′ |

A participant without a file of respondents, because the build failed or the files are missing, follows the second session on the slides: the GESIS terms do not allow a copy of the file to be passed on, so there is no other route.

In the session on the report, each participant opens the workspace, turns its folder into a repository with the completed preregistration block of Task 5 as the first commit, writes the report around the declared analysis, renders it from a clean session and commits each step. The file of respondents stays out of the repository: `data_private/` is ignored by git, and the GESIS terms do not allow it to be shared.

## The self-study route {#run-self-study}

The self-study track runs without a facilitator, and each stage page gives the total of its stage and nothing finer, because the time that a stage takes depends on the reader. The stages use the full deck of the case, `slides/eu-frames-full.qmd`, and a semester course can follow the same route in class. What the facilitator can still do for a self-study cohort is keep the live results pipeline running between deliveries, so that a result submitted alone appears on the Multiverse page of the case (`facilitator/live-results-setup.md`).

---

## Online and in-person cue sheet {#online--in-person-cue-sheet}

The materials are identical online and in person. What changes is how people answer, flag trouble and pair up.

| Beat | Online | In person |
|---|---|---|
| Quiz and waterfall answers | type in the chat, hold until "go" | write on paper, hands up on "go" |
| Working or stuck | green circle or "STUCK" in the chat | green or red sticky notes |
| Roll-call | "raise hand" | visual sweep |
| Pair moments | breakout rooms if available; a chat variant otherwise | table pairs |
| Rescues | buddy-chunk on the shared screen | the facilitator circulates |
| The live chart | everyone opens the Multiverse page themselves | projector and own laptops |
| Form links | pasted in the chat | QR codes on the slides |
| Breaks | countdown slide and "back at :xx" in the chat | countdown slide and spoken |

---

## Chat protocols and ready-to-paste texts {#chat-protocols-and-ready-to-paste-texts}

**Waterfall:** "Type your answer now but DON'T send – hold it. … Go." Holding the answers back keeps each one independent of the others. For Task 3 the answer is the analyst and the value, for example `KQXUE t = -7.169`, so that the wall of identical values appears once for each analyst.

**Help:** a STUCK in the chat is the first flag. The help document, a shared editable document whose link goes into the chat at the start, is the second place to look and the place where errors get pasted. Check it at the minutes that the run sheet names. Rescues run in the main room by buddy-chunk.

**Silent class:** wait 20 seconds, then take reactions as the minimal response, and name one or two people gently. Two substantive answers from twenty participants are enough to proceed.

**Catch-up card (paste at the start of Part 3):**

> Just back? You missed nothing you can't recover: (1) if Task 2 is unfinished, keep your estimand statement and come back to it later; (2) Task 3 is the reproduction – choose C6HJR, KQXUE or 018OL in the browser lab; each has a hint and a full solution, and the values on record are −3.804, −7.169 and −1.206; (3) flag STUCK and I'll come to you.

**Facilitator-drop standing order (seeded in the chat at the start):**

> If I drop off the call: keep going. The day plan (link) has the timings – finish the current task or take the break early. I will rejoin as soon as I can.

---

## Contingencies {#contingency-table}

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| **A participant's webR fails mid-task** | The cheatsheet ladder: hard reload and rerun the cells above, then a second browser, then buddy-chunk on my screen. Last rung: the specification is one row of `cases/eu-frames/data/spec_curve.csv`, which the download button on the Multiverse page serves; submit it by hand. |
| **The cell of 018OL stalls on its download** | Let it finish on a good connection, or switch the participant to C6HJR or KQXUE, which need nothing beyond the page. |
| **A participant's installation breaks** | Switch them to the browser lab, which holds every task; the workspace survives for later. |
| **The live chart fails** | Rung 1: `cases/eu-frames/multiverse.qmd` falls back to the committed `cases/eu-frames/data/class_results.csv`. Rung 2: pull the Sheet CSV, commit, re-render locally and share my screen. Rung 3: the static curve of 864 and the reference results are enough for the debrief. |
| **The OSF is slow or unreachable** | Show the dossier and the deposits on my screen. The data never depend on the OSF, because they ship with the browser lab and the workspace. |
| **"How long should this take?"** | Every fit on the 270-row panel is effectively instantaneous: `feols` with two-way or country fixed effects under 0.01 s; `try_spec()` in the workspace, CR2 test included, about 1 s for the first call, which loads the packages, and under 0.1 s after it; `try_spec()` in the browser lab instant, since it reads the curve that ships with the page. A participant who is waiting is waiting for a package download: the browser lab fetches its packages, about 24 MB, once when the page opens, a long moment on poor wifi, and nothing after that, because the Task 2 graph reads its adjustment sets from a table that ships with the page; the first run in the workspace installs the whole package set once. Ask what it is stuck on before assuming that the model is the problem. |
| **My connection drops** | The standing order in the chat. |
| **Recording objections** | Recording is optional, so stop it. |

## Expected numbers {#answer-keys-and-expected-numbers}

- Warm-up of Task 1: 1 = reproducibility (a failed attempt is still reproducibility); 2 = the grey area between reproducibility and robustness, argued both ways; 3 = replicability; 4 = generalisability.
- **Task 3, C6HJR** (`EUframes_cy.csv`, two-way fixed effects, conventional errors): b = −0.00347, SE = 0.00091, **t = −3.804**, df = 233, N = 270. Its conventional p is 0.0002, but under the rule of the course, CR2 errors clustered by country on 9.8 Satterthwaite df, p = 0.0504 (CR1 on 26 df 0.029; `cases/eu-frames/data/display_inference.csv`): not significant at 5% under that rule. Never call it significant without naming the errors.
- **Task 3, KQXUE** (`analyst_KQXUE.csv`, country fixed effects, conventional errors): b = −0.00736, SE = 0.00103, **t = −7.169**, df = 242, N = 270, CI from −0.00938 to −0.00533, as in the write-up of the analyst. With `cosmo_once` (EB 62.0 counted once) t = −7.166. On the Eurostat series as retrieved in 2026, in which Portugal 2013 reads 13.0 rather than 12.9, t = −7.172; the file uses the December 2023 vintage.
- **Task 3, 018OL** (`analyst_018OL.csv`, random intercepts for country, year and wave, Satterthwaite df): on the outcome rescaled to 0–1, b = −0.00203, SE = 0.00169, **t = −1.206**, df = 396.9, N = 420, as in the knitted output of the analyst; on the raw cell means b = −0.00072, SE = 0.00060, with the same t and df. With the year of the fieldwork for EB 79.3, t = −1.606. The default `parameters::model_parameters()` reports the residual df (414); `ci_method = "satterthwaite"` gives 396.9.
- **Hands-on 3b**: KQXUE, `task2.do`, `append using` the temporary file of EB 62.0 on two consecutive lines (441 and 442); 018OL, the line of the R Markdown file that sets `YEA` from the first four characters of the file name, commented "year of data collection"; C6HJR, the comment `# APRIL 2025 - Mistake in dataset here` in the corrected script of the fork. Good checks: no file read twice; one wave per fieldwork period with its expected count; counts by year and country; two builds compared cell by cell.
- The curve (`cases/eu-frames/data/spec_curve.csv`): 864 specifications; 98.1% below zero; 77.2% below zero with CR2 p < 0.05 (conventional 90.3%, CR1 80.1%); claim-aligned r from −0.589 to +0.116, median −0.314. Country fixed effects 92.6% below zero with CR2 p < 0.05, two-way 61.8%.
- Few clusters (`display_inference.csv`): two-way fixed effects t = −3.80 on 233 df conventional, −2.31 on 26 df with CR1 (p = 0.029), −2.23 on 9.8 df with CR2 (p = 0.0504); country fixed effects on the course panel t = −6.87 on 242 df, −3.62 on 26 df, −3.51 on 8.5 df (p = 0.0072). Within and between (`display_between_within.csv`): −0.0056 within, +0.0041 across the 27 country means (p = 0.31), difference p = 0.024.
- Reference results (`cases/eu-frames/data/reference_marks.csv`), each placed on the degrees of freedom of its own inference, with the number of the 864 further below zero: KEVF1 −0.452 (147); KQXUE −0.419 (214); OA −0.385 (267, the refit of its design without the education interactions, t = −8.39 on 403.9 Satterthwaite df); C6HJR −0.242 (583); PRL47 −0.176 (740); 018OL −0.060 (833). Multi100 recorded PRL47 at −0.006, its z converted on 394,575 respondents.
- Fork importance (`spec_curve_forks.csv`), share of the variance: estimator 41.5%, predictor 16.9, outcome 9.0, adjustment 4.3, item set 3.1, no-opinion rule 0.9, series 0.1, cell weighting 0.0, form 0.0, interactions 24.1.
- Placement of the reproduced specification (for participants without their own submission): 67%, with 583 of the 864 further below zero.

## Debrief questions {#debrief-question-bank}

Choose by what the class actually produced, not by the order below.

1. **The three reproductions**: "Three analysts, one claim, the same instructions: −1.2, −3.8, −7.2. Which difference between their models matters most, and how would you find out?"
2. **The slips**: "None of the three slips changed a conclusion. Does that make them unimportant? What would have to be true of a slip for it to matter?"
3. **The vintage**: "A public series changed after the analysis. Whose job is it to keep the version that a result rests on?"
4. **Decision that moved most**: "Before I showed the decomposition – which decision did you bet on, and what made the estimator carry so much?"
5. **Justification quality**: "Whose graph settled their choice? Whose graph could have justified three different specifications equally well?"
6. **Preregistration felt**: "Did completing the block before running change how the result felt when it landed?"
7. **The inference gap**: "If a curve-level permutation test came back at p = .30, what would survive of today? What if it came back at p = .004?"

## After the session

- [ ] After a workshop, run the reset procedure at the top of this guide.
- [ ] Export the feedback form responses.
- [ ] Improvement log: which segment ran longest; how the class split between the three analysts of Task 3, and how long the download of 018OL took on the connections of the class; whether the estimand statements showed real spread; how many people had the workspace running, and what that changed; which rungs of the contingency ladders fired.
